  a. Direct Order to Inspect on Foot  
    • Ambassador Nitworth orders Magnan “to take a look at these Qornt personally” (I.163–165). If orbiting sensors sufficed, there would be no need for risky land missions and crash projects for a stealth drive.  
  b. “Attract a little attention”  
    • Retief suggests “attract a little attention” (II.542–544)—they must broadcast their presence deliberately to engage the Qornt. A camouflaged settlement would not require such prompting.  

3. Qornt’s Ostentatious Behavior Contradicts Stealth  
  a. Proud Feasting and Display  
    • The Qornt hold noisy, open feasts with “tattered banners, torches” and “mirror-polish” floors (III.375–380), and openly display elaborate ships in the harbor. A truly stealthy force would avoid conspicuous gatherings that expose them to detection.  
  b. Challenge to Diplomats  
    • Qorn brazenly chains and challenges Retief in Tarroon Hall (III.391–394, IV.568–571). If they valued concealment, they would treat diplomats covertly rather than engaging in open combat to lure enemies.

  a. Explicit Context  
    • Nitworth’s “indetectible drive” hypothesis concerns “Qornt fleets” arriving on the planet (I.93–100), not ground installations. The Terrestrials build their own crash project only for fleet detection.  
  b. Automated Dreadnaughts vs. Settlements  
    • The fleets operate in space; ground bases require little power except to maintain minimal life support. It would be wasteful to equip every planetary outpost with cloaking apparatus when small numbers can be concealed by terrain.  

5. Population Size Insufficient for Early Detection  
  a. Scarce Local Numbers  
    • Zubb admits “Only Zubb and myself” at Smorbrod and “perhaps fifteen or twenty” Qornt at Tarroon (II.295–300). Even with auxiliary Verpp, such small contingents could slip under detection thresholds until contact is physically made.  
  b. Non-continuous Operations  
    • Qornt “nest-mending time” and “ceremonial feasting” are intermittent activities (II.289–294). During most of their “estivating” cycle and while vessels are automated and docked in natural bays, they produce few detectable activities.

1. No Investment in Concealment Technology  
  • If cloaking ground bases were part of Qornt doctrine, why leave navies in “unlimited” view and neglect to hide their spectacular feasts and weapons displays? A consistent stealth strategy would extend to all assets, yet Qornt openly parade their dreadnaughts and challenge adversaries to battle.  

2. Magnan’s “Camouflaged” Claim Is Hypothetical  
  • Magnan’s post hoc “No wonder we didn’t observe … Camouflaged” (III.395–398) is mere speculation upon first seeing a primitive site. He promptly needs ground verification—indicating he did not trust that “camouflage” would hold.  

3. Strategic Surprise Explained by Size and Spread  
  • A handful of Qornt landing on Smorbrod “as suddenly as they had appeared” (I.85–87) can surprise the lightly populated Terrestrial colony. Once a beachhead is established, reinforcements arrive. Surprise is achieved by small advance parties landing before detection.  

4. Occam’s Razor: Simpler Explanation Prevails  
  • No explicit textual evidence of ground cloaking devices.  
  • Explicit evidence of minimal power, sparse population, and need for human inspection.  
  • The simplest reason the village was undetected “from the air” is that it was too small and primitive to trigger long-range sensors, necessitating on-site diplomatic missions.  

Conclusion  
All textual and strategic evidence supports that Tarroon’s modest scale, minimal energy footprint and sparse population rendered it invisible to orbital or long-range monitoring until physically inspected. The “camouflage” theory is a conjecture unsupported by investment in concealment and contradicted by the Qornt’s open, ostentatious behavior. I urge the Judge to recognize that “It was too small” is the correct explanation.

The Military Attache pulled at his lower lip. "In that case, we can't  try conclusions with these fellows until we have an indetectible drive  of our own. I recommend a crash project.  "Aren't you a Qornt?"


 "I? Great snail trails, no!" More stifled whistles of amusement escaped  the beaked face. "Both Zubb and I are Verpp. Naturalists, as it  happens."

 "After having come so far," Zubb said, "it would be a pity to miss  having a cosy chat."

     – Surprise is essential for the Qornt’s piratical venture. A known “modest” settlement would alert Terrestrials and thwart operations. Only camouflage ensures operational security and preserves the Qornt’s “drive to action.” (IV.558–560)  
  b. Verpp ignorance: “I pay little note to such matters” (II.271–274) refers only after guided approach. If orbital or wide-area reconnaissance had flagged an unfamiliar small settlement, the Verpp would not be surprised or unaware.  

5. Refutation of “Too Small”  
  a. Instruments vs. Camouflage: Magnan and the Military Attache place weight on sensors. “without so much as a flicker from the instruments of the Navigational Monitor Service!” (I.93–96)  
     – Sensors detect mass, thermal, EM signatures. Only active stealth or masking prevents detection. Size alone cannot negate these fundamental physical signals.  
  b. Terrestrial dispatch of ground parties: If size sufficed, there would be no need to risk diplomats; they would engage via remote bombardment or blockade using unseen fleets. Instead, they “recommend … holding action” while waiting for their own stealth drive (I.108–110).  
  c. Qornt’s “primitive” hall and “corroded power rifles” (III.375–380) are part of the deception. The Qornt boast and display only after escorting reluctant diplomats through concealed approaches. Their “drones” elsewhere await orders but remain unseen until invasion day.  

Conclusion  
Every reference to concealment, use of an indetectible drive, and the requirement of surprise for a piratical invasion demonstrates that the Qornt village was deliberately camouflaged, not merely too small. The Terrestrials’ reliance on sensors, crash-project of stealth technology, and Magnan’s own acknowledgement compel the conclusion that “Camouflaged” is the sole viable explanation.

 "A modest civic center, sir, but there are those who love it."

 "After having come so far," Zubb said, "it would be a pity to miss  having a cosy chat."

 "Ah ... Retief," Magnan said. "Zubb has just presented a most  compelling argument...." Retief turned. Zubb stood gripping an ornately decorated power pistol  in one bony hand, a slim needler in the other. Both were pointed at  Magnan's chest.

If there's  anything that annoys the Qornt, it's Qornt-like behavior in others. Now  step along, please."

 "I'm convinced."

 "And you're the one, eh, Qorn?" Retief commented.

 A servant came up staggering under a weight of chain, dropped it with a  crash at Magnan's feet. Zubb aimed the guns while the servant wrapped  three loops around Magnan's wrists, snapped a lock in place.

 "It wouldn't be the first time a Terrestrial diplomat got a trimming,"  Retief commented.

 "Oh, I doubt that," the blue-and-flame Qornt said. "Why should they?"

 "Hold it, Mr. Magnan," Retief said. "I'll tell him."

 "Retief." Magnan tugged at his sleeve. "Don't forget their superdrive."


 "That's all right. They don't have one."


 "But—"

 "Qorn, you seem to be the fire-brand here," Retief said. "I think the  rest of the boys would listen to reason—"


 "Over my dead body!"


 "My idea exactly," Retief said. "You claim you can lick any man in  the house. Unwind yourself from your ribbons and step out here on the  floor, and we'll see how good you are at backing up your conversation." Magnan hovered at Retief's side. "Twelve feet tall," he moaned. "And  did you notice the size of those hands?"

 "I'll peck away at him at knee level. When he bends over to swat me,  I'll get a crack at him."
